method.label: Shift to base three and pair opposite values

annotationRationale: The coefficient shift gives a reversible correspondence with ordinary ternary expansions and proves that values are not duplicated. The multiplication principle counts the eight independent digit choices.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution: translate to ordinary ternary representations, then pair positive and negative values. The inverse digit shift makes uniqueness explicit.

review.mathCheck: The reversible shift b_i=a_i+1 gives unique eight-position ternary expansions, hence 3^8=6561 distinct values. Equivalently, shifting back by K=3280 gives every integer from −3280 through 3280. Including zero yields 3281 nonnegative integers, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded adaptation of the first MAA Q18 solution on page 8. It makes the constant translation, inverse digit map and sign pairing explicit.
review.annotationCheck: Uniqueness, completeness, leading zeros and inclusion of zero are all addressed. The argument is reconstructible at AMC 10 level.
